summary: Draft candidate package for AllowSystemRequiredPowerRequests under HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Power. The clean Win25H2Clean phase-0 batch confirmed the parent key exists while the value is absent on baseline, the repo power notes carry an exact docs hit with literal 1, the targeted current-build string batch found an exact ntoskrnl.exe Unicode hit, the shared mega-trigger runtime lane armed candidate value 1 but recovered without an exact hit, a retained local-KD disassembly pass shows the visible generic power-setting query/store layer operating through PopFindPowerSettingConfiguration, PopPowerSettingChangeStamp, and PopRegisteredPowerSettingCallbacks rather than a visible registry API, and a wildcard KD plus symbol-seeded Ghidra follow-up shows no visible `*PowerRequest*Reg*` helper while the only naturally resolved setting callback is the timeout-specific `PopPowerRequestExecutionRequiredSettingCallback`. New retained live-state and direct-reader passes now confirm `nt!PopPowerRequestConvertSystemToExecution = 1` and show `PopPowerRequestHandleExecutionEnablementUpdate` reading that global on the current build. A retained broad lightweight runtime lane also wrote the pair from baseline-missing to candidate value `1`, completed a real soft reboot, and still returned `no-hit` for the pair after reboot. A new retained retry audit over 10 mega-trigger runtime runs shows the pair repeatedly armed from baseline-missing to `1` and then exited `aborted-recovered` with zero exact hits on every parsed retry. A retained runtime path audit over the only current-build `path-hits.csv` capture found zero exact hits for the pair itself but 15 adjacent `Control\Power\PowerRequestOverride` accesses by `svchost.exe`, a new override-alignment audit ties those adjacent hits to the already-proven current-build override lineage, and a new power-setting trace-callback audit shows the visible generic setter registering `PopTracePowerSettingChange` rather than an exact pair-specific callback. A refreshed KVM guest-control audit now shows the dedicated narrow runtime runner is already wired, the qemu guest-agent channel is attached on the active libvirt domain, and a live bootstrap attempt installed the official qga MSI plus guest-tools MSI in the guest, confirmed a running `QEMU-GA` service and visible `VIOSERIALPORT` devices. A new live foreground repro then stopped `QEMU-GA`, observed host-side `guest-ping` fall back to `not connected`, and reproduced the stronger `QEMU guest agent is not available due to an error` state by launching `qemu-ga.exe -v -p \\.\Global\org.qemu.guest_agent.0` directly in an admin console. A later open-path probe then proved both `\\.\Global\org.qemu.guest_agent.0` and the exact registry-derived `...&02...` interface path are openable with `CreateFile`, and a follow-up exact-path foreground launch still reproduced the same host-side error/disconnected state while qga ran in a `debug: dispatch` loop. The candidate remains research-only because the earlier Control\Power seeding path and an exact post-boot read are still unresolved, and the live runtime-trace lane is currently environment-gated rather than runner-missing.

setting.name: Allow System Required Power Requests
setting.casual_explanation: This low-level Control\Power value appears to influence whether system-required power requests are converted into execution-required behavior inside the kernel power-request subsystem.
setting.why_people_change_it: Researchers track it when they want to understand how execution-required power requests are enabled, overridden, or collapsed into runtime power-request behavior.
setting.tradeoffs_overview: The candidate now has enough docs, static, and debugger evidence for a real draft package, and the visible current-build live state plus direct reader path are no longer open questions. A retained broad soft-reboot lane also exists, but it only narrows the missing layer to exact post-boot tracing rather than proving an exact rebooted read. The only retained runtime path-hit CSV currently lands on the adjacent `PowerRequestOverride` subtree rather than on the pair itself, that adjacent subtree now has its own override-lineage alignment proof, and the visible generic setter path now has explicit trace-callback proof rather than pair-binding proof.
setting.professional_notes: The Win25H2Clean 96-key phase-0 existence batch confirmed that HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Power exists while AllowSystemRequiredPowerRequests itself is absent on the clean baseline. Repo power notes document an exact literal of 1 and map the setting to PopPowerRequestConvertSystemToExecution. The targeted string batch on the current build found an exact Unicode hit in C:\Windows\System32\ntoskrnl.exe for the value name. A shared mega-trigger runtime lane then armed candidate value 1 for AllowSystemRequiredPowerRequests but the Procmon export recovered in an aborted state and did not yield an exact read. The retained local-KD power-setting query/store pass disassembled PopQueryPowerSettingUlong, PopGetPowerSettingValue, and PopSetPowerSettingValue. In the retained path, the generic power-setting subsystem acquires PopSettingLock, resolves configuration objects through PopFindPowerSettingConfiguration, updates PopPowerSettingChangeStamp, walks PopRegisteredPowerSettingCallbacks, schedules PopSetNotificationWork, and contains an explicit callback registration site that loads `PopTracePowerSettingChange` into `r8` before calling `PoRegisterPowerSettingCallback`. That retained callsite reinforces that the visible generic setter path is still notification/trace plumbing rather than an exact binding site for the execution-required pair. A second retained wildcard KD pass then showed no visible `nt!*PowerRequest*Reg*` symbols on the current build and only one `nt!*PowerRequest*Setting*` symbol: PopPowerRequestExecutionRequiredSettingCallback. The symbol-seeded Ghidra probe on that callback resolved only the timeout GUID path and found no direct or bounded indirect references to the callback symbol itself. New retained local-KD live-state proof now shows `nt!PopPowerRequestConvertSystemToExecution = 1`, matching the repo-doc enabled literal. A retained disassembly pass also shows `PopPowerRequestHandleExecutionEnablementUpdate` directly comparing `PopPowerRequestConvertSystemToExecution` against zero before it calls `PopPowerRequestEvaluateExecutionRequiredStatus`. A retained broad lightweight runtime lane then armed both execution-required values from baseline-missing to candidate value `1`, completed a real `reboot_mode=soft` cycle with healthy shell state before and after reboot, and still reported `no-hit` for both pair members in the post-boot batch result. The only retained current-build runtime `path-hits.csv` capture for this lane also stays adjacent: it contains zero exact hits for AllowSystemRequiredPowerRequests and AllowAudioToEnableExecutionRequiredPowerRequests, but 15 `svchost.exe` accesses under `HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Control\Power\PowerRequestOverride` covering the root, `Driver`, `Process`, and `Service` subkeys. A new alignment audit then ties those adjacent hits back to the already-proven override family in wildcard KD evidence: `PopPowerRequestHandleRequestOverrideQueryResponse`, `PopPowerRequestOverrideInitialize`, `PopUmpoSendPowerRequestOverrideQuery`, and `PopUmpoSendPowerRequestOverrideCleanup`, while the retained root dump also contains the `PowerRequestOverride` subtree. Together these follow-ups close the visible live-state and direct-reader gaps, while narrowing the runtime-trace story to an adjacent override lineage and a trace-oriented generic setter rather than exact pair reads. A refreshed host-side KVM guest-control audit then showed the remaining runtime lane is environment-gated in a narrower way: both execution-required records already map to the dedicated narrow path-aware runner, the live libvirt domain exposes the qemu guest-agent channel, and a live bootstrap attempt installed the official qga MSI plus the official `virtio-win-gt-x64.msi`, confirmed a running `QEMU-GA` service and visible `VIOSERIALPORT` devices, and rebooted the guest, yet host-side `guest-ping` still fails with `QEMU guest agent is not available due to an error` while the host-side controller stack remains vmrun-backed. A follow-up foreground repro then stopped `QEMU-GA`, observed host-side `guest-ping` fall back to `Guest agent is not responding: QEMU guest agent is not connected`, and reproduced the stronger `QEMU guest agent is not available due to an error` state by launching `qemu-ga.exe -v -p \\.\Global\org.qemu.guest_agent.0` directly in an admin console. The foreground console printed continuous `debug: dispatch` lines instead of a simple open-path failure, so the blocker now survives both the Windows service wrapper and an explicit expected-port launch. A later open-path probe then removed Windows path resolution as the leading theory: the guest can now open both `\\.\Global\org.qemu.guest_agent.0` and the exact DeviceClasses-derived `...&02...` interface path with `CreateFile`, while the `...&01...` sibling returns access denied and the naive `vport0p2` aliases still stay missing. A follow-up launcher then started `qemu-ga.exe -v -m virtio-serial -p <exact ...&02... path>` from the retained probe output, yet host-side `guest-ping` still returned `QEMU guest agent is not available due to an error` and HMP `info chardev` still showed the qga channel as `disconnected`. The remaining KVM blocker is therefore post-open qga runtime/protocol or libvirt/KVM handshake behavior, not path discovery. If this candidate is still registry-backed on the current build, the Control\Power seeding must occur earlier than the visible generic query/store, trace-callback, timeout-setting, direct reader, and adjacent override layers, or the post-boot window must be captured from a restored host-side guest-control surface with a narrower exact-read lane.

decision.why: AllowSystemRequiredPowerRequests now has exact repo-doc coverage, clean-baseline absence proof, current-build ntoskrnl string corroboration, a real trigger arm, retained local-KD proof that `PopPowerRequestConvertSystemToExecution = 1`, a direct current-build reader in `PopPowerRequestHandleExecutionEnablementUpdate`, a retained local-KD view of the generic power-setting query/store layer, retained wildcard/symbolized binding follow-ups, a retained broad soft-reboot runtime lane that still returns `no-hit` after reboot, a retained retry audit showing 10 mega-trigger runtime attempts all ending `aborted-recovered`, a retained path audit showing only adjacent `PowerRequestOverride` activity in the visible runtime CSV layer, a new alignment audit that ties that adjacent subtree back to the current-build override family, a new trace-callback audit showing the visible generic setter registering `PopTracePowerSettingChange` rather than an exact pair binding, and a refreshed host-side KVM guest-control audit showing the remaining narrow runtime lane is now blocked by a guest-side qga runtime/protocol failure after live bootstrap rather than by missing repo plumbing. A new live foreground repro strengthened that blocker by showing the failure survives an explicit expected-port launch. The later open-path diagnosis then closed the remaining path-resolution theory as well: both `\\.\Global\org.qemu.guest_agent.0` and the exact DeviceClasses-derived `...&02...` interface path are openable in the guest, yet restarting `QEMU-GA` or launching qga directly on the exact `...&02...` path still leaves host-side `guest-ping` in `QEMU guest agent is not available due to an error` and HMP `info chardev` in `disconnected`. The restored bootstrap ISO removes the missing-media issue and the guest now reaches a stronger post-bootstrap state, but the unresolved layer is now post-open qga runtime/protocol or libvirt/KVM handshake behavior rather than Windows path discovery, so that still does not restore live host-side execution on its own.
blocking_issues: The visible generic power-setting query/store layer is in-memory and callback-driven, but the earlier Control\Power seeding path into PopFindPowerSettingConfiguration objects or execution-required globals is still unresolved.
The only naturally resolved setting callback is tied to GUID_EXECUTION_REQUIRED_REQUEST_TIMEOUT and PopExecutionRequiredTimeout rather than to an exact AllowSystemRequiredPowerRequests binding site.
A retained broad soft-reboot lane now exists, but it still produced only batch-level `no-hit` rather than an exact post-boot read for AllowSystemRequiredPowerRequests.

A retained retry audit over 10 mega-trigger runtime attempts shows the trigger family is no longer missing; it repeatedly arms the pair from baseline-missing to `1` but still exits `aborted-recovered` without an exact registry read for AllowSystemRequiredPowerRequests.

The only retained current-build runtime `path-hits.csv` capture shows adjacent `Control\Power\PowerRequestOverride` accesses by `svchost.exe` and zero exact path hits for AllowSystemRequiredPowerRequests itself.

A retained alignment audit now links those adjacent runtime hits to the visible current-build override family rather than to an exact execution-required pair read, which strengthens the case that the missing layer is earlier seeding or a narrower exact-read lane.
A retained trace-callback audit shows the visible generic `PopSetPowerSettingValue` callback registration targets `PopTracePowerSettingChange`, not an exact execution-required pair binding site.

The dedicated narrow runtime lane is already mapped, and the active KVM session has the qemu guest-agent channel attached. Live bootstrap installed qga plus guest-tools, `QEMU-GA` can be started, the default alias `\\.\Global\org.qemu.guest_agent.0` is openable, and the exact DeviceClasses-derived `...&02...` path is also openable, but host-side `guest-ping` still fails with `QEMU guest agent is not available due to an error` and HMP still reports the qga chardev as `disconnected`. Even a foreground `qemu-ga.exe -v -m virtio-serial -p <exact ...&02... path>` launch reproduces the same failure, so the repo controller stack remains environment-gated by post-open qga runtime/protocol or libvirt/KVM handshake behavior rather than by missing path discovery.

open_questions: Is AllowSystemRequiredPowerRequests seeded earlier into execution-required state during boot or resume, or does the modern current-build family leave the Control\Power value absent while keeping only the in-memory global at `1` and the adjacent `PowerRequestOverride` subtree as the only visible runtime registry activity?
Should the remaining narrow exact-read lane be captured by restoring a KVM guest-control/bootstrap surface, or by executing the same repo-native runner from a vmrun-capable environment instead?
